messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @channel - multiple GPU hosts in pool 'serve-prod-2' reporting repeated Xid 13 / driver resets and container crashes. Alert rate spiked 2023-11-28T03:41:08Z. Suspected ECC/thermal faults, some nodes showing kernel oops. Please ack and start mitigation.

Becky Chen: acked. I'm on call. Observed increased 5xxs for /v1/generate and intermittent OOM kills on serving containers. Rolling error rate from 0.3% -> 6% in last 6m. Which customers impacted?

Samir Patel: seeing impact to prod-serving-1 (low-latency) and batch-embed-queue. Autoscale masked some errors but users see timeouts. I can pull logs from the suspicious nodes: gpu-node-17, gpu-node-19, gpu-node-21.

Maya Gupta: @Becky can you pin which node is currently hottest? I have telemetry showing thermal spikes on node-19: GPU temp jumping 83 -> 105C then driver reset. Might be sensor/firmware. Also ECC count increments on same GPU.

Becky Chen: thanks. Start triage steps: 1) cordon & drain affected nodes 2) route traffic off pool 'serve-prod-2' 3) enable fallback model variant in routing to keep latency SLOs. Samir can you coordinate drains?

Samir Patel: doing. Running:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-19
kubectl drain gpu-node-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
``` 
Draining gpu-node-19 now. Pods are rescheduling to serve-prod-1 and burst pool. Will monitor.

infra-bot: gpu-node-19 cordoned by Samir Patel at 1938502542. Drain triggered: 12 pods evicted. Health check redirect enabled for 3 routes.

David Li: attaching dmesg excerpt from gpu-node-19 prior to reset:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, pid=4321, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU appears to be lost
[ 1234.570124] kernel: NVRM: GPU panic: engine watchdog fire
[ 1234.571231] kernel: uut: ecc error threshold exceeded on GPU 0
```
Looks like repeated Xid 13. Also see `ceph` IO unrelated.

Maya Gupta: checking telemetry. ECC counts for GPU0 on gpu-node-19 increased by 700 in last hour. Thermal sensor reading shows short bursts to 105C. Could be failing fan or stuck frequency ramp causing thermal runaway.

Becky Chen: mitigate for now: 1) keep nodes cordoned, 2) continue reschedule, 3) disable high-power workload scheduling on pool (apply transient taint/label), 4) open ticket with colo/hosted vendor for hardware swap. Samir please set taint:
```bash
kubectl label node gpu-node-19 redwood/thermal-flag=hot
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-19 redwood/needs-inspection=true:NoSchedule
``` 

Samir Patel: applied taint and label. Patches for model routing in flight to avoid serve-prod-2 for new requests. Containers that crashed were restarted by K8s; some had `OOMKilled` in pod events and some showed `CrashLoopBackOff` with NV driver errors.

infra-bot: Added incident tag: gpu-xid-thermal-1938502468. Pager duty notified: oncall escalation to hardware. Estimated impact: medium (5-10% of global requests affected intermittently).

David Li: quick grep of driver logs shows repeated stacktrace pattern. Pasting snippet from /var/log/nv-host.log:
```
[ERR] ttm_bo_swap: dma_map error
[ERR] timeout waiting for engine idle
[WARN] ECC count 812 -> 1523
```
Not pure memory leak - looks like hardware ECC faults accumulating then watchdog triggers.

Maya Gupta: Suggestation: pin quantize fallback variant (lower perf) for affected customers to reduce thermal stress. Also increase cool-down window in scheduler to avoid hot-spotting same GPU.

Becky Chen: agree. Action items:
- Samir: finish draining gpu-node-17/19/21 and cordon the set (in progress) [inflight]
- David: upload logs to incident bucket and open hardware swap ticket with provider (include serials and ECC counts)
- Maya: adjust routing to fallback variants and throttle embeddings batch concurrency
- Becky: notify product & CS with impact blurb and estimated ETA for HW swap

Samir Patel: draining gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-21 now. gpu-node-21 had a container crash with NV driver reset then kubelet restarted container successfully. Moving pods to reserve pool.

Becky Chen: draft sent to CS: "We’re seeing intermittent GPU driver resets in a subset of serving hosts which can cause transient 5xx errors. We’ve taken the nodes out of rotation and are routing traffic to healthy pools. We're engaging hardware vendor for a swap. No data loss expected. ETA 2-6 hours depending on spare hardware." Please post updates in this thread for external comms.

David Li: vendor ticket created #HW-5732. Included dmesg, ECC counters, serial numbers and node inventory. Requesting expedited swap. Ticket ID and vendor tech assigned: felix@vendor. ETA 3 hours for onsite diagnostics.

infra-bot: cpu/gpu autoscaling adjusted for serve-prod-1 to accept temporary extra load; throttling rules applied to batch-embeds to preserve latency.

Maya Gupta: routing changes deployed. Fallback variant active for keys: prod-serving-1 and batch-embed-queue. Observed error rate drop from 6% -> 1.2% over 4 minutes.

Becky Chen: good. Monitoring for repeat resets on other nodes. If nodes show < 5 resets in 10m window, we'll uncordon after vendor signoff. Otherwise plan for full hardware replacement.

Samir Patel: all three flagged nodes cordoned and largely drained. A few long-running daemonsets remain; we'll evict safely during maintenance window. Current user impact trending down.

oncall-next: picking up handoff at 1938502945. Summary: multiple GPUs in serve-prod-2 triggered Xid 13/driver resets likely due to thermal/ECC hardware failures. Affected nodes cordoned and drained, routing fallback active, vendor ticket created (#HW-5732). Next steps: coordinate swap windows, verify new firmware+fans, run burn-in after swap. I'll watch overnight and post status updates. @Becky if anything changes ping me.

Becky Chen: thanks. handing off. Leaving runbook link and logs in incident doc. Closing active paging. :white_check_mark:
